comments.author: @EcuaLA
comments.text: Quito. The city where I was born in 1962. The city where my beloved Mother is buried since 2013. --- The American Dollar is the benchmark currency since 2000. Replacing the Ecuadorian SUCRE. --- My Mother said, in 2013, that her cab ride in Quito cost her $1 to anywhere in the city. Like a good son, I sent her $50 in cash singles, through the mail. To cover her cab rides. --- Clearly, prices in Ecuador are about 50 percent of prices in Los Angeles, California, USA., where I live. --- For everything, food, public transportation (especially the new Subway), housing. ---- I currently make $5000 per month fulltime ($60,000 per year),  in Los Angeles as a private chauffeur and rideshare driver, UBER/LYFT. --- But, the entire state of California is clearly overpriced. Blame the politicians for hurting the public. Not Helping the public. $5.50 for one gallon of gas. It used to be $2.50 for one gallon. . A small apartment in Los Angeles cost $2500 for a 600 square foot unit. ---- So, in comparison, Quito, is VERY AFFORDABLE. ---- LADRIVER.

comments.author: @MrCuriousPT
comments.text: Lo más importante en este tipo de comparación es entender que un salario promedio y un “costo de vida” nunca cuentan toda la historia por sí solos. 🇪🇨💵 Quito, Guayaquil, ciudades pequeñas y zonas rurales pueden tener precios completamente distintos, y vivienda, transporte o alimentación cambian muchísimo según el estilo de vida. Aun así, poner ingresos y gastos cotidianos uno al lado del otro ayuda a entender por qué para muchas familias llegar a fin de mes puede ser un desafío constante.
